subject: Acme Health: Request for EU-only serving + exclusion-zone routing playbook
messages:
From: Aisha Singh <aisha@acmehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Health Security <security@acmehealth.com>, Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 09:15:00 +0100
Subject: Request: EU-only serving + exclusion-zone routing playbook for PHI pilot

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are moving forward with a limited PHI pilot (clinical notes triage) and have one critical operational requirement before we can sign: all inference must remain in EU regions (data residency) and there can be no automatic fallback to non-EU model variants or cloud regions. For compliance and auditability we need a documented routing "exclusion zone" so requests from our tenant are never routed outside EU or to a model variant that isn't in the approved model list.

Attached: SOC2 scope extract and the initial SOW that references residency.

Questions for your team:
- Can Redwood enforce a tenant-level hard routing policy (region + model whitelist) that is non-overridable by autoscaler/fallback?
- If the runtime needs a degraded option (e.g., model variant not available), is there an approach for a controlled failure path (400-level) instead of fallback?
- What is the operational SLA/impact to latency and throughput if we pin to the EU GPUS and disable cross-region fallback?

We need to include this in the legal amendment, so a short technical write-up from Redwood about the playbook and expected impacts would help.

Appreciate a quick turn — our board review is 9/9.

Best,
Aisha Singh
Head of Data Products
Acme Health

Attachments: Acme_Scope_SOC2.pdf (pdf), Prod_SOW_Acme_8421.docx (docx)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Singh <aisha@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health Security <security@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: EU-only serving + exclusion-zone routing playbook for PHI pilot

Team — looping you in.

Short summary of the ask from Acme: they want tenant-level enforcement that prevents any cross-region routing or automatic fallback to non-approved model variants. They prefer explicit failure if capacity/model compatibility is missing rather than an automatic fallback. Board sign-off 2026-09-09, legal amendment required.

Karthik: what are the technical constraints if we implement a hard region + model whitelist at the routing layer? Specifically:
- Does our smart router support a tenant-level "no-fallback" flag today? If not, how invasive is the change?
- Can autoscaler still re-balance within EU-only pools? Any risk of cold starts causing failures?

Grace: we need a short operations playbook describing: policy enforcement points, expected latency delta, failure modes and recommended canary/rollout steps. Laura — please flag any legal/commercial impacts (SLA language, credits).

I'll reply to Acme acknowledging receipt. Can we aim for an internal tech note by EOD Wed (8/31) and a draft playbook by Thu (9/1)?

Thanks,
Rishi
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Singh <aisha@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health Security <security@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: EU-only serving + exclusion-zone routing playbook for PHI pilot

On Mon, Aug 30, 2026 at 11:02 AM Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — looping you in.
> 
> Short summary of the ask from Acme: they want tenant-level enforcement that prevents any cross-region routing or automatic fallback to non-approved model variants. They prefer explicit failure if capacity/model compatibility is missing rather than an automatic fallback.

Thanks Rishi — quick product/ops take below.

1) Feasibility (short answer): Yes. The router currently supports per-tenant routing policies (region preferences + model preferences) but the runtime has been designed for graceful fallback. A true hard "no-fallback" path requires:
   - a tenant-level flag in routing metadata (non-default)
   - a runtime change to short-circuit fallback and return an error code (we can implement as 409 or 503 with a specific error tag)
   - validation that autoscaler will only scale within EU pools (config-only; we already have GPU pool tags by region)

2) Risk and impact:
   - Latency: negligible for routing-layer checks; potential throughput impact if EU pool is capacity constrained (higher queuing)
   - Operational: increased risk of errors if regional capacity is saturated; we will need alerting and a runbook to respond (reserve burst capacity or dedicated pool)

3) Proposed compromise for pilot:
   - Implement tenant-level "exclude-other-regions" + model-whitelist immediately (config change)
   - Implement hard no-fallback behavior but gate it behind an "explicit_accept" flag (customer signs a short annex acknowledging potential service-level differences)
   - For the first 14 days, run a canary on 1% of traffic with identical config but allow shadowed monitoring to ensure error patterns are understood — no automatic fallback in canary.

Deliverables and timeline:
- Wed 2026-08-31 EOD: internal tech note (Karthik + Grace) describing change and required runtime bits.
- Thu 2026-09-01: draft "exclusion-zone playbook" (Grace) + runbook (ops) for capacity failures.
- Fri 2026-09-02: proposed SLA/annex text for legal (Laura) + short bullet list for Acme.

Action owners: Karthik (tech note + runtime estimate), Ops (runbook), Laura (legal annex), Rishi (customer comms).

Grace O'Connor
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: none in this message.

From: Aisha Singh <aisha@acmehealth.com>

Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: EU-only serving + exclusion-zone routing playbook for PHI pilot

Thanks Rishi/Grace — this is helpful and aligns with what our auditors expect. A few clarifications before we sign the annex:

- We accept the explicit_accept annex approach as long as the production behavior for our tenant is: hard enforcement of EU-only routing and explicit failure when the model isn't available (no transparent fallback).
- For the canary period we agree to the 14-day observation window; we do not want any fallback during canary.
- Please include an operational contact + escalation path in the playbook (phone + primary on-call).

Next steps we need from Redwood by EOD Fri (9/2):
1) The short tech note that Karthik mentioned (sufficient detail for our security team to review).
2) Draft annex language (Laura) that we can circulate to our procurement/legal.
3) Confirmation of expected latency impact under normal EU-only capacity assumptions (numbers or percentiles).

If we have those three items, we can proceed to sign and schedule the pilot for the week of 9/13.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — please reply-all with the deliverables when available.

Best,
Aisha Singh
Head of Data Products
Acme Health
